column2: Wash the spinach several times in plenty of water and chop finely.
Stir the tomato paste in the olive oil for 1 minute.
Add the boiled chickpeas and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the spinach and water; cook covered over low heat for 10 minutes.
Wash the rice and cook it with half a glass of water for 15 minutes until absorbed and soft.
Cook over low heat, stirring now and then, for 20 minutes until thickened.
Add the sugar and stir for 1 minute.
Don't add sugar under 2 years; after 2, no more than 1–2 teaspoons of added sugar a day is enough.
Divide into bowls and cover with cling film touching the surface; let cool.
Sprinkle with cinnamon when serving.
Break the cauliflower into small florets, boil for 5 minutes and drain.
Put in a small ovenproof dish; pour over the milk and sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes until the cheese is golden.
The cauliflower should be soft enough to crush with a finger.
Rest in the dish for 5 minutes to cool.
Wash the spinach in plenty of water and remove the stalks.
Blend the spinach, banana, egg and oats until smooth; leave for 5 minutes.
Rest on a plate for 5 minutes to cool.
Knead the mince and breadcrumbs and make walnut-sized flat patties; wash your hands.
Cook the meatballs in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 4 minutes on each side.
Wash the bulgur; dissolve the tomato paste in the water, bring to the boil and add the bulgur.
Cook covered over low heat for 12 minutes; turn off the heat and let rest for 10 minutes.
Break the meatballs into small pieces and arrange on the plate with the pilaf.
Wash and peel the carrot and apple; grate very finely.
Mix with the lemon; the apple won't turn brown.
Add the yoghurt and mix.
Don't give raw carrot as thick sticks or large pieces; it is a choking risk.
Peel the sweet potato and dice it smaller than the chicken.
Toss the chicken and sweet potato with the olive oil and thyme and arrange in a single layer on the tray.
Drain the tuna and flake it with a fork; remove any bits of bone.
Chop the corn finely.
Mix the lukewarm pasta, tuna, corn and yoghurt.
Limit canned tuna for children to 1 portion a week; choose tuna in water rather than oil, and a low-salt one.
Keep leftovers in a closed container in the fridge for 1 day; reheat only once.
Seed the pepper and chop very finely.
Whisk the eggs and milk and add the pepper.
Heat a non-stick pan over low heat and pour in the mixture in a thin layer.
Place the cheese and roll up; heat for 1 more minute.
When lukewarm, slice.
Break the broccoli into small florets, boil for 6 minutes and chop finely.
Mix the cooked rice, broccoli and milk and spread in the dish.
Sprinkle with the cheese and bake for 15 minutes until golden on top.
Wash and pick over the green lentils; boil in water for 20 minutes.
Peel the potato and carrot and dice them small.
Add the tomato paste and vegetables to the lentils; cook covered over low heat for 20 minutes.
Cut the chicken into small strips the child can hold.
Beat the egg in one bowl; mix the breadcrumbs and cheese in another.
Dip the chicken first in the egg, then in the breadcrumb mixture, and arrange spaced out on the tray.
Add the water; cook over low heat for 15 minutes until soft.
Add the milk and heat for 1 minute; don't boil.
Toast the bread lightly in a toaster or pan.
Spread the peanut butter in a very thin layer; a thick layer sticks to the palate and is a choking risk.
Slice the banana thinly and arrange on the bread.
Cut into four and serve.
Peanut is a common allergen; if giving it for the first time, start with a small amount and watch.
Whole or chunky peanuts must not be given before age 5.
Peel and dice the potatoes and add them with the water.
Cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes until the meat and potatoes are tender.
Chop the meat small to serve; no pink should remain inside.
Spread the cooked rice in a wide dish to cool quickly; keep it in the fridge.
Boil the peas and corn for 5 minutes and cool in cold water.
Chop the corn finely; mash the peas lightly.
Peel the cucumber and dice it small.
Mix everything with the olive oil and serve immediately.
Cooked rice can spoil if left at room temperature too long; don't leave it out for more than 1 hour, and eat within 1 day.
Add the egg, flour, cocoa and milk and whisk; leave for 5 minutes.
When cooked underneath, turn and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes.
Serve with chopped fruit.
Finely grate the carrot and squeeze out the liquid well.
Knead the mince, carrot and breadcrumbs; then wash your hands.
Add the milk slowly, stirring constantly so it doesn't go lumpy.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 5–6 minutes until thickened.
Add the sugar and stir.
Chop the chicken small; dice the carrot smaller than the chicken.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the chicken for 6–7 minutes until white.
Add the carrot and peas; add 3–4 spoonfuls of water.
Cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Mash the peas lightly and serve with rice.
Preheat the oven to 220°C; line the tray with baking paper.
Wash and finely chop the spinach; cook in a pan for 2 minutes until its liquid evaporates.
Roll the pide dough into a small oval and fold the edges inwards.
Spread the spinach, crack the egg into the middle and sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake for 12 minutes until the egg white and yolk are completely set.
Cool for 5 minutes and cut into small slices.
Peel and core the apples; dice small and spread in the dish.
Sprinkle the cinnamon over the apples.
Rub the oats and cold butter together with your fingertips until like sand.
Sprinkle the mixture over the apples.
Bake for 25 minutes until the apples are soft and the top is golden.
The apple should be soft enough to crush with a finger.
Add the linden and turn off the heat; steep covered for 5 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve.
Let cool and give no more than half a tea glass.
Don't add sugar or honey.
Ask your doctor before giving herbal teas to a child regularly; they don't replace water or milk.
